input.rationale: Refined the recovery-authority question from source reading before building its probe: a prepare reply whose Ballot differs from lastTriedBallot returns before being appended to lb.prepareReplies, so higher-ballot rejections never count toward SlowQuorumSize, no sub-case is selected at all, and the recovering replica emits no further message. This changes what the probe must observe (repeated identical prepares with no follow-up message, not a NOOP phase-1 restart).

investigations.hypothesis: makeBallot gives every non-designated replica a fixed recovery ballot (r.Id for the instance owner, r.Id+N otherwise), so a recovery whose accepting peers have a higher stored bal is rejected on every attempt: each reply returns before the quorum append, no sub-case is dispatched, no further message is emitted, and the periodic retry repeats the identical Prepare ballot; only r.IsLeader (set by the master's BeTheLeader RPC) lets the ballot climb above maxRecvBallot, after which the same call joins the higher ballot and reaches the sub-case dispatch.
investigations.discriminator: Whether two consecutive startRecoveryForInstance calls on a non-designated replica emit the identical Prepare ballot while every matching reply carries the peers' higher stored bal and the replica emits no PreAccept, Accept or Commit for that instance, and whether invoking the target's own BeTheLeader then produces a Prepare ballot above maxRecvBallot that the peers join (producing a matching reply and a dispatched sub-case).

knowledge.statement: In handlePrepareReply a reply whose Ballot differs from lb.lastTriedBallot increments lb.nacks and returns before the reply is appended to lb.prepareReplies, and the sub-case dispatch is guarded by len(lb.prepareReplies) >= SlowQuorumSize(); the only repair on the nack path (makeBallot plus a fresh bcastPrepare) is executed only while r.IsLeader is true.
knowledge.conditions: Recovery where the replicas that answer the Prepare have a stored bal above the recovering replica's fixed tried ballot, so every answer is a rejection rather than a matching-ballot reply (epaxos/epaxos.go:1204-1235, with epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451 and 1216-1235).

knowledge.statement: makeBallot assigns the instance owner the ballot equal to its own replica id and any other recovering replica id+N, and advances it in steps of N only while r.IsLeader is true and the candidate is below maxRecvBallot; epaxos.New hardcodes IsLeader false and only the exported BeTheLeader RPC sets it, which the master invokes for the replica it designates.
knowledge.conditions: Any startRecoveryForInstance call in the captured snapshot, including repeat calls from executeCommands after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451, 1127-1150, 149-165, 1121-1125).

investigations.question: When a replica that does not itself hold the value recovers instance (replica A, instance i), does the recovery adopt the value that prepare replies report as accepted/pre-accepted, or does it replace that value with a NOOP?
investigations.hypothesis: startRecoveryForInstance sets inst.vbal to the newly tried ballot and puts its own PrepareReply (VBallot = that ballot, Status/Command from its own possibly empty local state) first into lb.prepareReplies; the adoption loop only takes replies with VBallot >= the running candidate ballot, so genuine replies at the real value ballot are skipped and the recovery proceeds to sub-case 6 with a NOOP command.
investigations.discriminator: Whether a permitted execution can reach recovery at a replica whose crtInstance[A] >= i while its own instance holds no command (no pre-accept, e.g. it only received an Accept because the pre-accept peer set and accept peer set differed); and whether the emitted PreAccept after recovery carries Command NOOP while a delivered prepare reply carried the accepted command at a lower vbal.

gaps.question: Does a permitted execution produce a recovery coordinator that knows instance (A, i) (crtInstance[A] >= i) but holds no command for it, so that the fabricated self-reply decides the adopted value? Candidate: an Accept-phase broadcast to a different peer set than the PreAccept broadcast (peer liveness change between the two broadcasts at the leader) lets a replica learn the instance with Status NONE and Cmds nil.

history.discriminator: Whether a permitted execution can reach recovery at a replica whose crtInstance[A] >= i while its own instance holds no command (no pre-accept, e.g. it only received an Accept because the pre-accept peer set and accept peer set differed); and whether the emitted PreAccept after recovery carries Command NOOP while a delivered prepare reply carried the accepted command at a lower vbal.

investigations.question: Can a recovering replica that is not the master-designated leader recover an instance whose accepted value sits at a ballot above its own recovery ballot, or does the periodic retry repeat the same rejected prepare with no enabled repair?
investigations.hypothesis: makeBallot gives a fixed ballot per replica (r.Id for the instance owner, r.Id+N otherwise) and climbs above maxRecvBallot only while r.IsLeader is true; epaxos.New hardcodes IsLeader false and only the master's BeTheLeader RPC sets it, so for every other replica a prepare at its fixed ballot is rejected by any acceptor whose stored bal is higher, and the three nack repairs (handlePreAcceptReply, handleAcceptReply, handlePrepareReply) are all gated on r.IsLeader. executeCommands re-enqueues the same instance every COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD, so the same rejected prepare is repeated without a ballot advance, and instances that depend on the stuck instance cannot execute.
investigations.discriminator: Whether two consecutive startRecoveryForInstance calls on a non-designated replica emit the identical Prepare ballot while the acceptors' replies all report a higher stored ballot, with no higher-ballot Prepare emitted and the instance uncommitted; and whether the same call on a replica with IsLeader true emits a ballot above maxRecvBallot.

knowledge.statement: startRecoveryForInstance places the recovering replica's own state into lb.prepareReplies as a PrepareReply whose VBallot is the newly tried recovery ballot (inst.vbal is overwritten with lb.lastTriedBallot), while its Status/Command come from the recovering replica's own instance, which for a replica that never pre-accepted is Status NONE with Cmds nil.
knowledge.conditions: Any call to startRecoveryForInstance (epaxos/epaxos.go:1127-1168), including calls made from executeCommands for uncommitted instances up to crtInstance[q] after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD (epaxos/epaxos.go:404-417).

knowledge.statement: handlePrepareReply adopts a reply's Command/Seq/Deps/Status only when reply.VBallot >= the running candidate ballot, starting from lb.ballot = the pre-recovery local vbal and evaluating the coordinator's own self-reply first; replies whose VBallot is below that running value leave lb.cmds/lb.status unchanged. lb.status == NONE then selects sub-case 6, which calls startPhase1 with state.NOOP() because lb.cmds is nil (only the self-reply's value would have replaced it).
knowledge.conditions: Recovery of instance (replica, instance) by a replica whose own state has no pre-accepted command, when all remote replies carry a value ballot below the coordinator's freshly tried ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1236-1313).

result.summary: Refined the recovery-authority question by source reading before building its probe, and promoted two behaviors. handlePrepareReply returns on a mismatched ballot before appending the reply to lb.prepareReplies, so higher-ballot rejections never count toward SlowQuorumSize and no sub-case is dispatched at all - the recovering replica emits no PreAccept, Accept or Commit rather than restarting phase 1 with a NOOP; the only repair on that nack path (makeBallot plus a fresh bcastPrepare) is gated on r.IsLeader. Separately, makeBallot fixes a replica's recovery ballot at r.Id for the instance owner and r.Id+N otherwise, advancing only while IsLeader is true and the candidate is below maxRecvBallot, with epaxos.New hardcoding IsLeader false and only the master's BeTheLeader RPC setting it. The question's hypothesis and discriminator were updated to match: the probe must observe repeated identical Prepare ballots with no follow-up message, and then invoke the target's own BeTheLeader to see the ballot climb above maxRecvBallot and the sub-case dispatch run. The probe scenario is designed but not yet written and executed; the probe for the value-adoption question remains complete with its executed witness and executed control.
